changes_made.explanation: Added missing baseline models that are explicitly compared in the experiments. Expanded outputs to better reflect the paper's focus on bilingual lexicon induction and cross-lingual embeddings.

Removed metrics that are part of the model training/optimization process rather than evaluation metrics. Only kept Accuracy@1 which is the actual evaluation metric used to measure performance on the bilingual lexicon induction task.
No LLM-based evaluation is used in this paper. The paper focuses on bilingual lexicon induction using traditional methods without any LLM involvement.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. All evaluations are based on automatic metrics (Accuracy@1) using ground truth bilingual dictionaries.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI), which is a specific sub-task of machine translation involving word-level translation rather than full sentence generation. The paper proposes two semi-supervised frameworks (CSS and PSS) and evaluates them using Accuracy@1 metric on standard BLI datasets. The extraction was generally accurate, but needed refinement on metrics to distinguish between training objectives and evaluation metrics.
